findings.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14-19 — record_for_host does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` without lowercasing the right-hand `host` value (from `uri.host`, not case-normalized), so any stored host with uppercase characters (permitted by the case-insensitive `/i` format regex, and not downcased in `before_validation`) will never match at request time, silently breaking embedding for those hosts (confidence 90, P1).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-6 — the `host` column has no unique index (and no `validates_uniqueness_of` in the model either), so admins can create multiple embeddable_hosts rows for the same host mapped to different categories, and `record_for_host`'s `.first` makes the effective category binding non-deterministic (confidence 85, P1).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-6 — no index at all on `host`, even though `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` performs a `lower(host) = ?` lookup on every single embedded request, turning a hot request-path check into a full table scan as the table grows (confidence 80, P2).

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:15-18 — `record_for_host` matches only `uri.host` (port stripped by `URI#host`) against the stored `host` value, while the model's own validation regex (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) explicitly permits storing a host with a port suffix like `example.com:8080`; any host saved with a port can never match an incoming request, a format-drift between what admins are allowed to store and what the lookup actually compares (confidence 80, P1).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — `category_id` is `null: false` with a `belongs_to :category` association but no DB foreign key constraint and no index, so category deletion can silently orphan embeddable_hosts rows (dangling category_id) with no referential-integrity guard at the schema level (confidence 70, P2).

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — `validates_format_of :host` allows an optional trailing path segment (`(\/.*)?`) even though `before_validation` already strips everything after the first `/`, meaning the regex's path-matching branch is dead/inconsistent with actual stored data, indicating the schema for what "host" means was not fully thought through (confidence 55, P3).

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:322 — no uniqueness validation (model or DB index) on `host`, so admins can create duplicate host rows mapped to different categories and `record_for_host`'s `.first` will nondeterministically pick which category new embedded topics land in (confidence 75, P2).

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:326-329 — `before_validation` strips scheme/path from `host` but never downcases it, while `record_for_host` (embeddable_host.rb:338) compares with `lower(host) = ?` against the incoming (not-necessarily-lowercased) `uri.host`, so a stored mixed-case host (e.g. "ExAmple.com") can silently fail to match a same-host referer with different casing, breaking the embed allow-list for that host (confidence 60, P2).

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:322 — `belongs_to :category` has no `validates :category, presence: true` and no DB foreign-key/dependent-destroy handling, so if the referenced Category is later deleted the embeddable_host row is left pointing at a nonexistent category_id, and `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(...).try(:category_id)` in topic_embed.rb:400 will pass a dangling id into PostCreator with no fallback to uncategorized (unlike the create/update controller path, which does fall back) (confidence 60, P2).

app/models/topic.rb:379 — `expandable_first_post?` dropped the prior `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` gate entirely instead of replacing it with an equivalent `EmbeddableHost.exists?` check, so the sibling flag that used to gate expandability on "any embeddable host configured" is silently removed rather than migrated, changing behavior for sites that later remove all embeddable_host rows but still have old topic_embeds (confidence 50, P3).

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:265-267 — `save_host` accepts any `category_id` from the client (via `category-chooser`) with no check that the category is not read-restricted/private, so an admin can point an allowed embed host at a private category and anonymous embedded-feed topic creation (topic_embed.rb, skip_validations: true) will create a topic in a private category without any acknowledgement/warning in the admin UI (confidence 50, P2).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:524-527 — the new `embeddable_hosts` table has no unique index on `host` and no NOT NULL/format constraint enforced at the DB layer beyond `null: false`, so the completeness of the model-level validation (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb has no create/update/destroy behavior specs at all — only a subclass check) is unverified: there is no test exercising validation failures, duplicate-host rejection, or category fallback-to-uncategorized behavior (confidence 75, P1).

spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:1-9 and spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:1-9 — both new controller specs only assert the class hierarchy (`< Admin::AdminController`) and add zero coverage for create/update/destroy actions, permission enforcement, or the category_id-blank-falls-back-to-uncategorized logic in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:267, leaving the core admin CRUD feature functionally unverified by tests (confidence 100, P1).

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `t.string :host, null: false` but no unique index, and the model `EmbeddableHost` only has `validates_format_of :host` (no uniqueness validation). This means the UI/controller can create multiple rows with the same normalized host (the `before_validation` strips scheme/path) potentially pointing to different `category_id`s. Lookup uses `record_for_host` -> `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so with duplicates the chosen row/category is dependent on DB row order and can be non-deterministic, affecting `TopicEmbed.import` which uses `eh.try(:category_id)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-6 — no index at all on `host`, even though `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` performs a `lower(host) = ?` lookup on every single embedded request, turning a hot request-path check into a full table scan as the table grows (confidence 80, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `t.string :host, null: false` but adds no index on `host` (or a functional index on `lower(host)`). Meanwhile `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` / `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` on requests, so this lookup is on a request path. This is a performance/scalability concern grounded in the diff, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:15-18 — `record_for_host` matches only `uri.host` (port stripped by `URI#host`) against the stored `host` value, while the model's own validation regex (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) explicitly permits storing a host with a port suffix like `example.com:8080`; any host saved with a port can never match an incoming request, a format-drift between what admins are allowed to store and what the lookup actually compares (confidence 80, P1).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and then compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. `URI#host` excludes the port, but the model’s `validates_format_of :host` explicitly allows an optional `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` port suffix, and the `before_validation` normalization strips protocol and path but does not strip a port. Therefore an admin can save `example.com:8080`, which will never match an incoming request like `http://example.com:8080/...` because lookup compares only `example.com` against stored `example.com:8080`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — `category_id` is `null: false` with a `belongs_to :category` association but no DB foreign key constraint and no index, so category deletion can silently orphan embeddable_hosts rows (dangling category_id) with no referential-integrity guard at the schema level (confidence 70, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `t.integer :category_id, null: false` but does not add an index on `category_id` or any DB-level foreign key constraint to `categories(id)`. The model `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` has `belongs_to :category`, so the association exists at the app layer, but nothing in the diff enforces referential integrity in the database. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:61 — `ensure_embeddable` authorizes the entire embed_controller (comments/count, CSRF-exempt via skip_before_filter :verify_authenticity_token) solely by checking `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`, but the Referer header is fully attacker-controlled from any non-browser HTTP client (curl/requests/Postman), so anyone can forge `Referer: http://<allowed-host>/` to bypass the embeddable-host restriction entirely and pull topic content directly, defeating the feature's only access-control guarantee (confidence 100, P2).

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` the diff shows authorization is reduced to `raise ... unless EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (replacing the previous SiteSetting-based check). Because this decision is based solely on `request.referer`, any client that can set arbitrary HTTP headers can spoof an allowed Referer value and satisfy `host_allowed?`, effectively bypassing the host restriction for the embed endpoints. The diff does not show any additional non-Referer validation added here to prevent that.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:10-19 — `record_for_host`/`host_allowed?` only compares the parsed URI's hostname (`uri.host`) against the stored `host` column, even though the model's format validator (line 2) permits admins to restrict a path suffix (e.g. `example.com/allowed-path`); any path/subpath restriction an admin configures is silently ignored at authorization time, so a Referer of `http://example.com/anything` is allowed even when the admin intended to scope it to `/allowed-path` (confidence 75, P3).

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, any path suffix an admin enters is stripped before validation via `before_validation` (`self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), so the model does not actually support storing path-scoped allowlist entries. Additionally, `record_for_host` compares `uri.host` to the DB `host` column (`where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), so if a path *were* stored (e.g. via the migration’s raw SQL insert), it would *not* match and would deny rather than “silently allow any path”. The diff therefore doesn’t show an authorization bypass where `example.com/allowed-path` unintentionally permits `example.com/anything`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:11-21 — `record_for_host` returns `false` (not `nil`) on invalid/blank host, an inconsistent sentinel type mixed with legitimate ActiveRecord `nil` results from `.first`, and no spec directly tests this method's return values (only indirectly through embed_controller_spec's response status), so callers using `.present?` happen to work today but a future caller checking `.nil?` specifically would silently misbehave and no test would catch it. (confidence 75, severity P2)

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, `record_for_host` explicitly returns `false` for malformed/blank input (`return false unless uri.present?` / `return false unless host.present?`), but returns `nil` when no DB row matches (`where(...).first`). This mixes sentinel types (false vs nil) for “no record” outcomes. Current callers (`host_allowed?` uses `.present?`, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)`) won’t break, but a future caller using a strict `.nil?` check could mis-handle invalid input. Specs added only cover `host_allowed?`, not `record_for_host`’s return semantics directly.
